verdict.rationale: The only first-party signal is a GitHub claim of covering 96% of the web, including JS-heavy pages, with "no proxy headaches." That implies proxies are managed for you, but nothing shows a developer can choose premium residential or datacenter proxies. A community comment says Firecrawl and Firecrawl Simple lack a proxy service. That comment likely refers to the open-source or self-hosted builds, so it adds doubt but is not a concrete contradiction of the hosted claim. Missing for 10: documented proxy-type options (residential vs datacenter or a premium tier), any API parameter or docs for proxy selection, and independent hands-on confirmation that hard-to-scrape sites are bypassed.
